newsitem.title: USA: Wheels Sports sees charge from game.
newsitem.headline: Wheels Sports sees charge from game.

text.p: Wheels Sports Group Inc said Tuesday that it expects to post a third quarter charge of about $400,000 as part of its decision to cease operations of its Fantasy World Racing interactive game.

The company said it has decided to shut down the game, which is played through the telephone, fax and the Internet, because it was not generating the revenues it had expected when it launched it in February.

The game divided the NASCAR Winston Cup series into three seasons and offered participants the chance to compete for cash awards during each season by accumulating points based on pole and final race results. Operations are to cease at the conclusion of the game's second season, August 23.

"Revenues from Fantasy World Racing did not meet our expectations during the game's first two seasons, and the start-up costs associated with the game have negatively impacted the company's financial results," Chairman, President and Chief Executive Howard Correll said in a news release.

"Since going public in April 1997, Wheels has acquired other NASCAR-related businesses which we believe provide better growth opportunities than Fantasy World Racing," Correll said. "Our program of growth through acquisition will continue to provide us with additional opportunities. We believe that shifting our resources and energies to these potentially more attractive businesses is in the best interests of the company and its shareholders."

Start-up costs associated with the game were about $525,000 during the first six months of 1997, while revenues from the game were about $120,000, Wheels said. The company said it anticipates recording a third-quarter charge of about $400,000 for the discontinued operations.
